html:
The Iran-Iraq War was fought from September 1980 to August 1988 between Iraq and Iran. It was one of the longest and deadliest wars of the late 1900s, and it ended with the border where it began.

Saddam Hussein invaded Iran in September 1980. He hoped to use the chaos after the Iranian Revolution to take the Shatt al-Arab waterway and the oil province of Khuzestan, and to stop the revolution spreading to Iraq's own Shia majority. Iran held, and by 1982 had pushed the Iraqis out.

Ruhollah Khomeini then refused peace and carried the war into Iraq. It became a war of trenches like the First World War:

  • Iran sent waves of young volunteers against Iraqi lines.
  • Iraq used chemical weapons against Iranian troops and against its own Kurds, as at Halabja in 1988.
  • Both sides fired missiles at each other's cities and attacked oil tankers in the Gulf, which drew in the US navy.

Most Arab states and the West backed Iraq. In July 1988 Khomeini accepted a UN ceasefire, saying it was like drinking poison. Hundreds of thousands died. The war hardened the Islamic Republic, and it left Iraq deep in debt, especially to Kuwait, which Saddam invaded in 1990.
sum: The Iran-Iraq War was fought from September 1980 to August 1988 between Iraq and Iran. It was one of the longest and deadliest wars of the late 1900s, and it ended with the border where it began.
